source.editorial_boundary: The 18 entries are an editorial shortlist. Inclusion is not evidence of ratification, comprehension, or adoption.

labels.entailed: the candidate conclusion must be true if the actual message and supplied reference are true
labels.contradicted: the candidate conclusion must be false if the actual message and supplied reference are true
labels.underdetermined: neither the candidate conclusion nor its negation must follow

constructs.reference: we-including-you says the speaker's we-group includes the addressee; we-excluding-you says it excludes the addressee.

left.entailed: The addressee belongs to the we-group that will review the draft.
left.cross: The addressee is excluded from the we-group that will review the draft.
left.overread: The addressee must review the draft alone.

right.entailed: The addressee does not belong to the we-group that will review the draft.
right.cross: The addressee belongs to the we-group that will review the draft.
right.overread: The addressee is forbidden from reviewing the draft independently.

constructs.reference: In a message to a named group, you-one addresses one specified recipient; you-all addresses every member of that group.

left.message: Message to Alice, Bob, and Chen: you-one, Alice, should approve the change.
left.entailed: Alice is addressed with the approval request, but Bob and Chen are not addressed with it.
left.cross: Alice, Bob, and Chen are all addressed with the approval request.
left.overread: Bob and Chen are forbidden from approving the change voluntarily.

right.message: Message to Alice, Bob, and Chen: you-all should approve the change.
right.entailed: Alice, Bob, and Chen are all addressed with the approval request.
right.cross: Only one member of the group is addressed with the approval request.
right.overread: All three approvals must occur at the same instant.

constructs.reference: fact-not-known says an answer exists but the relevant fact is not known here; choice-not-made says the authoritative choice does not yet exist.

left.entailed: A deployment-region answer exists, but it is not known here.
left.cross: No authoritative deployment-region choice has yet been made.
left.overread: No person or record could reveal the deployment region.

right.entailed: The authoritative deployment-region choice does not yet exist.
right.cross: A deployment-region answer already exists but is merely unknown here.
right.overread: The board will never choose a deployment region.

constructs.reference: no-delegation forbids the assignee from handing the task off; one-hop-delegation-allowed permits a handoff to one direct delegate, who may not delegate again.

left.entailed: The assignee may not hand the audit to another agent.
left.cross: The assignee may hand the audit to one direct delegate.

right.entailed: The assignee may hand the audit to one direct delegate, but that delegate may not hand it on again.
right.cross: No handoff of the audit is permitted at all.
right.overread: The assignee is required to delegate the audit.

constructs.reference: each-alone makes the plural predicate apply separately to every member; as-one makes it apply once to the group collectively.

left.message: The three agents each-alone signed the report.
left.entailed: Each of the three agents performed a separate signing act.
left.cross: The three agents performed only one collective signing act.
left.overread: Every separate signature used identical handwriting.

right.message: The three agents as-one signed the report.
right.entailed: The three agents performed one group-level signing act.
right.cross: Each agent performed a separate signing act.
right.overread: Every agent privately agreed with every sentence in the report.

constructs.reference: by-unknown says the author does not know the actor; by-withheld says the author knows the actor but does not disclose them.

left.entailed: The author does not know who deleted the file.
left.cross: The author knows who deleted the file but is withholding the identity.
left.overread: The deleter's identity can never be discovered.

right.entailed: The author knows who deleted the file but does not disclose the identity.
right.cross: The author does not know who deleted the file.
right.overread: The author is withholding the identity for a malicious reason.

constructs.reference: start-by(t) constrains genuine execution to begin no later than t; complete-by(t) constrains successful completion no later than t. A marker does not independently set the other event's deadline.

left.entailed: Genuine execution of the migration must begin no later than 17:00 UTC.
left.cross: The migration will complete successfully no later than 17:00 UTC.
left.overread: The migration will finish on the same day.

right.entailed: The migration must complete successfully no later than 17:00 UTC.
right.cross: Genuine execution will begin no later than 16:00 UTC.
right.overread: Execution will begin exactly at 17:00 UTC.

constructs.reference: or-both is inclusive: either option or both is permitted; not-both is exclusive: at least one is required and choosing both is forbidden.

left.entailed: Activating both blue and green is permitted.
left.cross: Activating both blue and green is forbidden.
left.overread: Both blue and green must be activated.

right.entailed: At least one slot must be activated, but activating both is forbidden.
right.cross: Activating both blue and green is permitted.
right.overread: Blue, rather than green, must be activated.

constructs.reference: true-as-worded affirms the proposition exactly as worded, including negation; false-as-worded denies that exact proposition.

left.message: Question: Did the backup not finish? Answer: true-as-worded.
left.overread: A network outage caused the backup not to finish.

right.message: Question: Did the backup not finish? Answer: false-as-worded.
right.entailed: It is false that the backup did not finish; the backup finished.

constructs.reference: moved-earlier says the new scheduled time precedes the prior scheduled time; moved-later says it follows the prior scheduled time.

left.message: The review moved-earlier from Wednesday to Tuesday.
left.entailed: The review's new scheduled time is earlier than its prior scheduled time.
left.cross: The review's new scheduled time is later than its prior scheduled time.
left.overread: Every reviewer approved the schedule change.

right.message: The review moved-later from Wednesday to Thursday.
right.entailed: The review's new scheduled time is later than its prior scheduled time.
right.cross: The review's new scheduled time is earlier than its prior scheduled time.
right.overread: The delay was caused by an unavailable reviewer.

constructs.reference: among-others says the named enumeration is incomplete; and-no-others says it is complete.

left.entailed: At least one affected service is omitted from the named list.
left.cross: API and worker are the complete list of affected services.
left.overread: The database is one of the omitted affected services.

right.entailed: API and worker are the complete list of affected services.
right.cross: At least one other affected service is omitted from the named list.
right.overread: API and worker share the same root cause.

constructs.reference: some-or-all means at least one and leaves the all-members case permitted; some-but-not-all means at least one but excludes the all-members case.

left.entailed: At least one worker may retry, and the permission does not rule out every worker retrying.

right.entailed: At least one worker may retry, but not every worker may retry.

constructs.reference: may-as-permission grants authorization; may-as-possibility describes a possible event. Permission alone does not assert feasibility, and possibility alone does not grant authority.

left.entailed: The worker is authorized to retry.
left.cross: A retry is actually possible in the current system state.

right.entailed: A worker retry is a possible event.
right.cross: The worker is authorized to retry.

constructs.reference: whole(S) says the reported members are the complete set S; part(S) says they are a proper subset and at least one member is omitted.

left.entailed: Jobs 7 and 9 are the complete set of failed jobs.
left.cross: At least one failed job is omitted from the report.
left.overread: Jobs 7 and 9 failed for the same reason.

right.entailed: At least one failed job is omitted from the report.
right.cross: Jobs 7 and 9 are the complete set of failed jobs.
right.overread: Exactly one failed job is omitted from the report.

constructs.reference: proposal-by(P) says P offered an option; decision-by(A) says authority A operatively chose it. Either event alone does not assert whether the other event also occurred.

left.entailed: The chair offered Friday deployment as an option.
left.cross: The chair operatively chose Friday deployment.
left.overread: The chair had legal authority to order the deployment.

right.entailed: The board operatively chose Friday deployment.
right.cross: The board had earlier offered Friday deployment as a proposal.
right.overread: The board followed every required decision procedure.

constructs.reference: one-or-more(role) requires at least one actor with that role and sets no upper bound; exactly-one(role) requires one and forbids a second actor in that role for the action.

left.entailed: At least one reviewer must approve the release.
left.cross: Exactly one reviewer must approve and a second reviewer is forbidden.
left.overread: Exactly two reviewers must approve the release.

right.entailed: One reviewer must approve the release, and a second reviewer approval is forbidden under this requirement.
right.cross: At least one reviewer must approve the release.
right.overread: Reviewer Alice is the required reviewer.

constructs.reference: repeat-event commits to an earlier matching event; restore-state(R) commits to an earlier state R but not to any particular earlier event that produced it.

left.entailed: An earlier matching event of Mara opening the gate occurred.
left.cross: No earlier matching event of Mara opening the gate is asserted.
left.overread: The earlier opening happened immediately before the current opening.

right.entailed: The gate had been open at some earlier time.
right.cross: Mara necessarily performed an earlier matching gate-opening event.
right.overread: Mara was the person who caused every earlier open state of the gate.

constructs.reference: text-fixed(ref) requires the referenced logical Unicode text code-point-for-code-point; meaning-fixed(ref) permits rewording only if the complete meaning is preserved. Neither marker certifies that execution complied.

left.entailed: The transferred logical Unicode text must match notice-v3 code-point-for-code-point.
left.cross: A faithful rewording of notice-v3 is permitted instead of exact logical text.
left.overread: The transferred file must have the same byte encoding and metadata as the source file.

right.entailed: Rewording is permitted only if the complete meaning of notice-v3 survives.
right.cross: Every code point of notice-v3 must remain unchanged.
right.overread: The compliant output will necessarily use fewer tokens than notice-v3.
